title: an ambient Error declaration introduces no runtime binding, so nothing may be emitted that names it

xfail.reason: The reference compiles this with zero diagnostics and then the emitted module dies while it is still loading: `ReferenceError: Ambient is not defined`, exit 1. It emits `__vsRegisterError(Ambient, "smithers:...:Ambient")` for an ambient class declaration, and an ambient declaration introduces no runtime binding, so the registration is a reference to nothing. A clean compile that cannot run is the failure mode this is filed against. The Go fork skips ambient declarations at the registration site only — its SMITHERS1150 duplicate-name refusal is unchanged, so an ambient class still reserves its identity and two same-named ambient Error classes still collide — and prints `ok`. This is the one place the two backends deliberately differ. Retire the marker when the reference stops emitting a registration for a declaration that has no runtime binding.

notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Error Classes': "The compiler MUST provide stable nominal identity, matching metadata, serialization evidence, and cross-realm transport metadata while preserving ordinary `Error` behavior." The obligation is about classes the compiler emits; `declare class` emits nothing, and the last clause — preserving ordinary behavior — is violated outright by a program that cannot load.
